title: No Verified Incident Can Support Dog-Trade Defenses
excerpt: No verified incident, court record, seizure, or health alert appears in supplied material. Honest reform needs public records, quarantine, and abolition by 2030.
body_html:
No police seizure, court judgment, intercepted shipment, or emergency health alert appears in the material available for this dispatch. That leaves no verified incident to describe—and no honest basis for claiming that stolen companions, cyanide bait, or uninspected meat caused a named event. Invented heartbreak would serve neither Vietnamese families nor animals.

Records must replace slogans

“Tradition” cannot verify animal origin, lawful transport, quarantine, veterinary inspection, or protection against theft. “Farm-raised dogs” cannot stand as proof without traceable records, licensing, health documents, and enforcement reports. The supplied material names no official dataset, police case, court file, or government notice establishing those facts.

Research task status remains unresolved. That link is not evidence of a seizure, conviction, outbreak, or supply-chain practice. It is a processing record.

Public safety needs precise action

Rabies exposure generally occurs when infected saliva enters a bite, scratch, broken skin, or mucous membrane. After possible exposure, wash the wound with soap and running water for at least 15 minutes and seek urgent medical care. Post-exposure prophylaxis includes vaccination and, when indicated, rabies immunoglobulin or approved monoclonal antibodies. Once clinical symptoms appear, rabies is virtually 100% fatal. Household exposure incidents and commercial supply chains remain separate questions; neither should be linked without primary evidence.

Vietnamese families, pet guardians, veterinarians, and local leaders deserve transparent records and enforceable quarantine—not unsupported assurances. SDE calls for complete abolition by 2030. Sign the national petition and add your name to that public demand.
